Subject: Payment route confirmation & trial gatekeepers

Hi Samira / Oliver —

Great talking with you earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook going into procurement: 

Call recap (high level)
- Trial scope: 3-week pilot focused on real-time inference for triage workflows (up to 200k tokens/day peak).
- Trial goals: validate latency SLOs in your infra, measure cost per session, and confirm model quality on 3 benchmark prompts you shared.
- Primary stakeholders: Samira (Procurement), Oliver (Platform), Marcus (CS lead at Redwood), me (AE).

Open items for procurement path decision
1) Preferred payment route: PO (net-30 invoicing) vs. company card vs. AWS Marketplace listing. Each has different lead time and billing model — we need your preference so we can align the quote and legal docs.
2) Paper process: if PO, please share procurement contact + PO template and any mandatory clauses (COPPA/HIPAA redlines if applicable).
3) Trial-to-paid trigger: recommend we either (A) start billing on an agreed calendar date, or (B) start billing when trial hits a usage threshold (we suggested 50k billed tokens) or explicit written sign-off. Please state which you prefer.

Suggested next steps (short timeline):
- You: confirm payment route and procurement contact by EOD Fri (2026-10-01).
- Us: send a trial plan + quote that matches chosen payment route (attached: redwood-trial-plan-template.pdf and a preliminary quote).
- Procurement: if PO, target PO issuance by 2026-10-07 to hit the trial start window the week of 10/10.

Success criteria (proposed, can change):
- Latency: p95 < 450ms on your staging infra for 512-token responses
- Availability: >99% for test window
- Quality: >= 80% pass rate on the 3 benchmark prompts you provided

Attachments: redwood-trial-plan-template.pdf, quote_BBH_RBW-2026-141.pdf

If you want, Marcus can join the procurement thread to walk your finance team through our invoicing and SOC controls — he can also provide a short checklist for legal.

Thanks,
Tessa

Hi Samira — copying Marcus (CS) and Tessa (AE) so we can unblock procurement quickly. Short answers/notes below: 

1) Invoice cadence / terms- We support Net-30 invoicing for PO customers; invoices issued monthly in arrears unless you elect milestone billing. We accept ACH and wire.

2) Agreement flow- For pilots under $50k we typically do a short pilot addendum (one page) attached to our standard MSA. For larger pilots we do a full MSA. Signing authority: Redwood signs via our legal counsel (I can get the signature block pre-filled). If you need an executed MSA first, we can prioritize that but it adds ~3-7 business days.

3) AWS Marketplace- Marketplace purchases allow consolidated billing under your Marketplace contract and are generally faster for procurement that leverages marketplace agreements. Note: pricing/credits are handled through Marketplace; we can walk through benefits but it does require vendor onboarding on their side.

4) PO template & remittance- Please send your PO template. In the meantime attaching our procurement-checklist.xlsx with the exact remittance fields and required billing address to speed review.

SOC2 / DPA: Marcus will drop links in a follow-up. For PHI-adjacent use cases we can discuss a scoped DPA and any required security addenda; if you expect PHI we should flag that now so legal can review.

Operational recommendation (to meet your timeline)
- If you need to start the pilot the week of 10/10 and procurement can’t commit to a PO by 10/07, consider starting on a company card or via a short trial addendum while procurement issues a PO. That prevents losing the engineering window.

Attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

- We will proceed with a PO. I have the procurement team assigned and they expect to issue the PO by 2026-10-07 (internal approvals permitting).
- Trial start: aiming for 2026-10-11 (engineering availability).
- Billing: our preference is to start billing on 2026-11-01 (one month after trial start) unless we hit the usage threshold earlier; please keep billing triggers explicit in the quote.
- Success criteria: we confirm the three benchmarks (latency p95 < 450ms; availability >99%; accuracy pass rate >=80%).

Next steps — procurement will request your remittance info and the PO template. Marcus, please share the SOC2 report and DPA link directly to procurement@brightbridgehealth.com.
